learning_outcomes: Take a short brief to a finished image through defined stages
Use stage checks (reads at small size, clear focal point) before moving on
Budget time per stage and finish pieces
Compare your process with that of professional artists and studios
Review your own work after a delay and note what to change

resources.title: FZD School of Design: free articles and Design Cinema (Feng Zhu)
resources.free_notes: The school's page says Design Cinema is a YouTube channel offering free tutorials and industry knowledge, and lists free blog posts. The school itself is a paid one-year diploma programme. I could not open the Design Cinema Notion page or confirm specific episodes.
resources.notes: Blog posts named on the page: Sketching 101, Line Art Fundamentals, Fundamentals of Design, Top 10 Tips for Designers, For Students: Learning Perspective. The school's own channel is https://www.youtube.com/@FZDSCHOOL (concept design tutorials for games and film; I confirmed the channel exists but no specific videos). The three programme terms on the page (fundamentals, expanding the visual library, story-driven portfolio) are a handy map of the whole workflow.

resources.title: Marco Bucci YouTube channel
resources.free_notes: The channel is free. His paid material includes lessons at marcobucciartstore.com, a 22-lesson Proko course 'Illustrating Children's Books (and beyond!)' ($59; lesson 20 'Painting Final Art' runs 48:25 and is premium) and 'From Fundamentals to Finished Paintings with Marco Bucci' on Creature Art Teacher.
resources.notes: The channel description says it covers painting fundamentals, applied painting demos and insights into growing as a creative person, with experience in film, TV, games and print. I could not fetch playlists or specific video titles, so choose from the Playlists tab.

resources.title: Gurney Journey: Preliminary Sketches and Imaginative Realism labels
resources.free_notes: Blog is free and a January 2026 post says it runs with no paywalls. Permissions allow non-commercial quoting with credit.
resources.notes: Preliminary Sketches had about 75 posts and Imaginative Realism about 53 when checked. Pick posts that show a sequence of stages.

resources.title: Blender Studio: Spring open movie production material
resources.credit: Andy Goralczyk and the Spring team
resources.free_notes: Some articles are tagged Free; a related training page needed a login and a membership of 11.50 euros per month. I could not confirm whether the gallery is free.
resources.notes: A real short-film production: concept art, character design, storyboard samples, model sheets, previz images, production logs and a 48-minute staff-file breakdown listed in the gallery. Use it to compare a professional pipeline with your own.

practice.title: Brief to finish in stages
practice.description: Write a three-line brief. Produce 12 thumbnails, 3 value roughs, 1 tonal sketch, a colour pass, then a finished piece, noting time spent at each stage. Spread across sessions if needed.

practice.title: Reference round
practice.description: Collect 30 references and note five decisions the references changed in your design.

practice.title: Stage-gate checklist
practice.description: Before leaving each stage, check: reads at stamp size, one clear focal point, silhouettes distinct, no tangents, value groups clear. Write a tick or cross per stage.

practice.title: Compare with a pro process
practice.description: Open a production page and compare its stages to yours, noting one thing to copy and one thing to avoid.

practice.title: Delayed review
practice.description: Wait a day, look at the piece fresh, and write three lines: what works, what does not, what you would change next time.

done_when: You have completed one piece from brief to finish with record of each stage
You can state the time you spent per stage and which stage over-ran
Your final piece keeps the focal point and silhouette decisions made at thumbnail stage
You have compared your workflow with a professional example and changed one habit
common_mistakes: Rendering before the composition is settled
Skipping reference and thumbnails and starting at the final size
Giving no time limit per stage, so early stages swallow the whole project
Never finishing because you keep restarting
